## How GRACE Follow-On Tracks Changes in Earth’s Water

GRACE Follow-On consists of two satellites that follow one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart. As they pass a larger concentration of mass, gravity affects the leading satellite first, initially pulling it farther from the trailing satellite and changing the distance between them.

That change in separation is used to infer shifts in mass. Scientists use those inferred shifts to investigate changes in Earth’s water, including groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers and ice sheets, and sea level changes attributable to water added to the oceans.
